'''''Triglochin scilloides''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Lilaea scilloides''''', is a [[species]] of [[aquatic plant]]s [[Native species|native]] from western Canada to Mexico, and to western and southern South America. It has been introduced into [[Portugal]] and [[Spain]].<ref name=POWO_77110106-1/> English names include '''flowering quillwort'''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Please verify |url=https://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi/auth/challenge?return_to=/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=91083 |access-date=2026-04-02 |website=ucjeps.berkeley.edu}}</ref> At one time, it was the only species accepted in the genus '''''Lilaea'''''.<ref name=POWO_Lilaea/>

==Description==
''Triglochin scilloides'' is an annual herb growing in or just next to water in several types of shallow aquatic habitat, including [[vernal pool]]s, [[mudflat]]s, streams, ponds and ditches.<ref>{{Cite web |date=February 2015 |title=Phylogeny, biogeography and evolution of Triglochin L. (Juncaginaceae) – Morphological diversification is linked to habitat shifts rather than to genetic diversification |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1055790314003650?casa_token=gDRVroz_2ioAAAAA:QDDqPZCYENaETYPfrM7mjwu8lUcNmY9M8QZ9ZOIE00BVdOUG06mTmlYtEKEJdheaKwxO_aJtLdQ |url-status=live |access-date=3 April 2026 |website=ScienceDirect}}</ref> The plant takes the form of a tuft of basal leaves around a very short stem. Each onionlike leaf is very narrow, long and pointed, reaching 25 to 40 cm long. It is wrapped in a translucent sheath at the base. The [[inflorescence]]s include clusters of [[stamen|staminate]] and [[plant sexuality|bisexual flowers]] at the tip of a narrow stalk as well as [[gynoecium|pistillate]] flowers in underwater axils. The pistillate flower is composed of a threadlike [[Style (botany)|style]] which may be up to 30 cm<ref>{{cite book | last= Heywood | first= V.H. | date= 1978 | title= Flowering Plants of the World |location= New York | publisher= Mayflower Books | page= 82 }}</ref> long tipped with a stigma which floats on the water surface. The fruit is a beaked, ribbed nutlet up to 1 cm long.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}}

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described in 1804 by [[Jean Louis Marie Poiret]], as ''Phalangium scilloides''. In 1925, it was moved to the genus ''Lilaea'' as ''Lilaea scilloides'',<ref name=POWO_77110106-1/> where it was accepted at one time as the only species in a [[Monotypic taxon|monotypic]] genus.<ref name=POWO_Lilaea>{{Cite web |title=Search for 'Lilaea' |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/results?q=Lilaea |access-date=2024-03-23}}</ref> In 2010, it was moved to ''Triglochin scilloides'', the name accepted by [[Plants of the World Online]] {{As of|2024|March|lc=yes}}.<ref name=POWO_77110106-1/>
